1. Outside view. The series has a base rate of moving about 0.58 net points week-to-week, though recently it has seen stronger directional drops. Over the last four weeks (July 17 to August 14), the tracker moved from -21.5 to -24.2, averaging a decline of roughly 0.67 points per week. A naive extrapolation based on this recent trend would suggest a drop to around -24.9. 

2. Inside view. The primary driver of the recent drop is the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran and associated economic or inflationary concerns, leading to declining approval for Trump. Polling from mid-August (including a Reuters/Ipsos survey released August 17) emphasizes that his approval has fallen to 33%, matching historical lows from his first term. Civiqs’ smoothed MRP model is likely to continue pricing in these sustained low ratings. Assuming the bad news cycle persists and continues to slowly drag down the smoothed estimate, another drop is highly likely, though perhaps decelerating slightly as it approaches a historical floor. A drop of 0.4 to 0.5 points brings us to -24.6 or -24.7.

3. Pre-mortem. If this forecast is badly wrong, it is most likely because the tracker hit a "floor" where nearly all easily persuaded voters have already defected, causing the rating to flatten out or even experience a slight mean-reverting bounce (as happened in mid-July when it briefly rose to -21.5). To correct for this, I won't extrapolate an accelerated plunge, but rather predict a moderate decay with a standard deviation wide enough to encompass a stabilization around -24.2 or a steepening drop toward -25.5.

4. Calibrate. The series changes by 0.58 points on average week-to-week. Assigning a standard deviation of 0.6 ensures that a typical 1 SD interval (e.g., -24.0 to -25.2) cleanly captures the range of most likely outcomes, accounting for both a plateau and a continued decline.
